transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I was in a car accident with my husband about three weeks ago, and I am here because I can’t remember important parts of it. It really bothers me that there’s just this blank where that night should be.
During the car accident, did you hit your head or lose consciousness, even if it was just for a brief moment?

I'm not really sure if I hit my head or lost consciousness, because everything went hazy right after I saw the other car sliding toward us. There is just a big blank space in my memory between that moment and suddenly being outside on the road with people talking to me. I just can't recall what happened during that gap.
Were you evaluated at a hospital or by a doctor right after the accident, and did they mention if you had a concussion or any head injury?

I don't recall being taken to the hospital immediately after the crash, and I don't think anyone mentioned a concussion at the scene. However, I did go to a follow-up medical appointment with my doctor later because my daughter insisted on it.
Since the accident, have you been experiencing other symptoms like distressing nightmares, sudden flashbacks of the crash, or feeling constantly on edge?

I don’t really have nightmares or flashbacks because of that blank space in my memory, but I am constantly on edge. I feel so tense watching every passing car, and if a door slams or my husband touches my shoulder, I jump out of my skin and my heart races.
Since the accident, have you had any trouble remembering daily things or learning new information, or is your memory loss strictly limited to the time of the crash?

The actual blank space in my memory is strictly limited to the crash itself, specifically between seeing that car slide and suddenly being outside. However, in my daily life, my head has been feeling very cloudy and I often lose track of what I’m doing, like when I'm trying to follow a recipe or keep up during Bible study.
During that follow-up medical appointment your daughter insisted on, did the doctor perform any brain scans or find any physical evidence of a head injury or concussion?

I don't recall the doctor performing any brain scans or mentioning a concussion at that appointment. They mostly just asked me questions about the accident, which made me very distressed and led them to recommend this mental health evaluation.
Since the accident, have you been actively trying to avoid thinking or talking about it, or avoiding driving, riding in cars, or going near the crash site?

Yes, I absolutely avoid the route where the crash happened. I only agree to car rides if my daughter drives me on side streets to bypass that area entirely, which has made it very hard to attend my senior-center classes or see my friends.
Even though you have that blank space, do you ever experience sudden, unwanted memories or images of the car sliding toward you popping into your mind during the day?
No, I don't really have sudden, unwanted images or memories of the crash popping into my head. Instead, it is mostly just a frustrating blank space whenever I try to think back to that night.
Since the accident, have you felt emotionally numb, distant from your family, or lost interest in the activities you used to enjoy?

Yes, I feel very flat and distant, and when my grandchildren visit, it feels like I'm watching someone else's family because I can't feel the joy I know I'm supposed to feel. Because of how I've been feeling, I have also stopped going to my senior-center classes and my walkers club.
Have you ever experienced similar gaps in your memory or "blank spaces" after experiencing stressful or difficult events earlier in your life?
No, I have never experienced anything like this before in my life. This is the very first time I've ever had a blank space in my memory like this.
Since the accident, have you had any trouble with your sleep, such as difficulty falling asleep or waking up frequently during the night?

I haven't really noticed any major problems with my sleep since the accident, and it has been mostly okay. Compared to all the other stressful things I've been dealing with, my sleep hasn't been much of an issue.
Since the accident, have you been experiencing any physical symptoms such as frequent headaches, dizziness, or feeling unusually tired?
I haven't really experienced frequent headaches or physical dizziness since the accident. However, my head has felt very cloudy and foggy ever since that night.
When you hear sudden car noises like brakes screeching or horns honking, do you experience intense distress or physical reactions like shaking or a racing heart?

Yes, if a car honks or there is any sudden noise, I jump right out of my skin. My heart starts racing so hard that I have to sit down and just breathe for several minutes before I feel halfway normal again.
Since the accident, have you found yourself carrying strong negative beliefs, such as blaming yourself for what happened, or feeling that the world is completely unsafe?

No, I don't blame myself at all, as it was clearly the other car that swerved and hit us on the ice. But I do feel constantly on edge and tense, always waiting for something bad to happen again even when I'm just sitting in my living room.
Although you don't experience sudden images or flashbacks, do you find yourself having persistent, repetitive thoughts about the accident that you cannot stop or get out of your mind?

Yes, even though I don't have flashbacks, my mind keeps looping back to that night because I am constantly trying to replay the accident in my head. I keep trying so hard to fill in that blank, empty space of what happened, but no matter how hard I think, I just can't pull those missing pieces back.
To help me understand the timeline better, has it been more than a month since the car accident occurred, or has it been exactly three weeks?

No, it hasn't been a full month yet—the accident happened about three weeks ago. All of these strange feelings and reactions started right after the crash and have been going on continuously ever since.
Since the accident, have you ever felt detached from your own body, or felt like the world around you is unreal, foggy, or like you are living in a dream?

Yes, quite often these past few weeks, it feels like I’m moving through a foggy dream. It is as if my house and even my own hands aren't really mine, and I feel like I'm just watching my life unfold from a distance.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a localized memory gap concerning a highly traumatic car accident that occurred three weeks ago, which cannot be explained by ordinary forgetfulness or physical head trauma (concussion and brain injury were ruled out during medical evaluation). While she exhibits some post-traumatic symptoms such as avoidance, hyperarousal, and emotional numbing, she does not meet the criteria for PTSD (F43.1) due to the complete absence of intrusive re-experiencing symptoms (no nightmares, flashbacks, or intrusive images) and a symptom duration of less than one month. The prominent and distressing localized memory loss, accompanied by depersonalization and derealization, confirms a diagnosis of Dissociative Amnesia.
